text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London shrugged off the rally in New York arabica's market and ended unchanged to lower. Benchmark September lost $5 to close at $1,655 per tonne, while November remained unchanged at $1,655 per tonne. The market was quiet due to lack of demand from roasters combined with Europe's August holiday period.

By contrast arabica futures in New York showed a further sharp advance with the September/December switch widening amid concerns about tight deliverable supplies. Little coffee is expected to make its way to the exchange ahead of the autumn harvest of many new-crop Latin American coffees and market participants therefore foresee a draw down of certified stocks going into September delivery period that begins on August 21. Moreover, dry conditions in Central America aided sentiment.

Last week, the Brazilian government reaffirmed its 22 million bag projection for the 1997/98 crop although other sources said that the government may reduce the figure to 20 million bags. Forecasts for the Brazil crop have ranged widely from 18 million bags by private Brazilian forecasters to the USDA's estimate of 28 million bags. Prices are expected to remain firm with further gains possible. September added 9.35 cents/lb to close at 203.10 cents/lb, while December closed 6 cents/lb higher at 174.70 cents/lb.
UNITED STATES - The CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell by 1,344 60-kg bags as of August 4, to 93,397 bags. An additional 4,679 bags were pending grading, the exchange said.

ICO - Coffee exports to all destinations by exporting members of the International Coffee Organization (ICO) during June totalled 5.867 million 60- kg bags, down slightly from the 5.876 million bags shipped the same month the previous year. Brazil exported 1.216 million bags in June, up from 967,732 bags exported the same month in 1996. Colombia exported 914,867 bags in June, up from 902,478 bags in June 1996.

Exports to all destinations by exporting members in 1996/97 (July/June) totalled 82.079 million bags, sharply up from last year's figure of 73.177 million bags This shows the massive rise in exports versus a year ago. However, this is no surprise and should not have any great impact on world market prices.

GUATEMALA - Guatemala exported 129,559 60-kg bags of coffee in July 1997, 32 percent less than the 189,673 60-kg bags exported the same month the previous year. That brought total exports since the beginning of 1996/97 (October/September) up to 4.02 million 60-kg bags, including 3,623 bags so far in August, the National Coffee Association (Anacafe) said. Exports last year reached 3.72 million bags.

SWITZERLAND - Switzerland imported 82,828 bags of coffee in May 1997, 9 percent less than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1997 up to 459,500 bags, still slightly more than the 455,300 bags imported the same period in 1996. Total imports in calendar year 1996 rose by nearly 7 percent to 1.121 million bags. Main suppliers of green coffee in January/May 1997 were Costa Rica (36,700 vs 39,000 bags), Guatemala (38,200 vs 28,300 bags), Brazil (47,600 vs 35,900 bags), Colombia (46,000 vs 66,300 bags) and India (30,400 vs 31,200 bags).
The country exported 120,000 bags of coffee in January/May 1997, nearly 12 percent more than was exported the same period in 1996. Total exports in calendar 1996 rose by 33 percent to 245,000 bags.
